title: Downy Oak: Ancient Downy Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Usually a modest, crooked oak of dry hillsides. The Bátaszék oak on a Hungarian vineyard hill was voted Europe's Tree of the Year in 2016.
intro: Downy oak is the tree dry limestone hillsides are made of, usually a modest, crooked field-edge oak that loses out to better species on good ground, so a big one is worth the detour. The most famous stands on Orbán Hill above the wine town of Bátaszék in southern Hungary, hollow, 4.7 metres round and put at 300 to 400 years. In 2016 it was voted Europe's Tree of the Year, and every 25 May locals pour wine over its trunk for a good harvest. Umbria grows the species on every slope. Outside Assisi, the oak of Via di Valecchie went onto Italy's national register in July 2026 as the tallest monumental tree in the region, thirty metres up. Near Perugia two grow 150 metres apart within eight centimetres of the same girth, on ground the species shares with truffles.
